findings.title: Light-theme color for embedded post author links was changed incorrectly
findings.body: The original light-theme value for `.embedded-posts .topic-meta-data h5 a` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but this change uses `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` as the first `dark-light-choose` argument. This makes the link substantially dimmer in light themes, rather than preserving existing light-theme behavior while adding the dark-theme alternative. The first argument should remain 30% (with the appropriate secondary-based dark value).

findings.title: Group member names no longer preserve their light-theme emphasis
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new light-theme branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%)`. This changes the appearance in light themes even though the intended change is to use `$secondary` for dark themes. Preserve the 30% primary lightness in the first branch and add the corresponding secondary-based dark branch.

findings.title: Mobile group member names use the wrong light-theme lightness
findings.body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` rule had a 30% primary lightness before this PR, but now selects a 50% primary lightness in light themes. As a result, mobile light-theme member names lose their previous visual emphasis. Keep `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` as the light branch while adding the secondary-based dark branch.

findings.title: Modal message-length hint reverses its intended light-theme contrast
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but the newly added light-theme branch is `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. This alters light-theme hint text rather than only fixing dark-theme rendering, and makes it much darker than before. Retain the 70% primary branch and choose the appropriate secondary-derived value for dark mode.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading lost its original light-theme color
findings.body: The `.topic-map h3` rule originally used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`, but this change substitutes a 50% primary light-theme value. This is an unintended light-theme regression; the desktop counterpart preserves 20% and uses 80% secondary for dark mode. The mobile rule should likewise keep the 20% primary branch and use the secondary-based dark branch.
